metaDescription: Six countertop microwaves listed at or below $100, from a 0.6 cubic foot dial model to 1000 W family units, compared on watts, capacity and controls.
expertTake: The Farberware 1.1 is the top pick for 1000 W and a dinner plate sized cavity. The COMFEE 0.7 is the value pick for reheating. Skip the 700 W units if you cook rather than reheat, since they are slow and uneven.
introParagraphs: At this cap a microwave can reheat well, but cooking is a stretch unless you pay attention to wattage. Most units here sit at 700 to 1000 W, and the gap between them is larger than it looks on the box.

This guide compares size and power first, then controls and safety. We favour units that match their wattage to their cavity and that state their dimensions. Prices move, so the $100 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Farberware countertop microwave 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W
products.description:
The Farberware 1.1 is a 1000 W microwave with ten power levels and multi stage cooking. It has six preset buttons and a stainless steel finish. It hits the wattage sweet spot for full meals.

At 1.1 cubic feet it holds a standard dinner plate. It is a good value family size. At 1000 W and 1.1 cu ft it outpowers the 700 W COMFEE and fits a dinner plate.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Before relying on the Farberware 1.1 microwave for a week of meals, run a cup of water for one minute and check how hot it gets, then adjust package times to its wattage.
products.bestFor: Families who want 1000 W at a modest size

products.name: TOSHIBA microwave oven 0.9 cu ft, 900 W, 6 auto menus
products.description:
The TOSHIBA 0.9 delivers 900 W output on 1400 W input and offers six auto menus, a mute function, a child lock and LED lighting. Its dimensions are 18.7 by 13.3 by 10.7 inches. The mandatory two step child lock helps with young children.

It is compact for a 900 W unit. Its auto menus give one touch cooking. Its 900 W and mute function come in a smaller body than the Farberware.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Place the TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave with clear space around it and a stable, level surface, since blocked vents and an uneven turntable are common causes of poor results.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that want 900 W and a mute

products.name: BLACK+DECKER countertop microwave 0.9 cu ft, 900 W

specList.label: Presets
specList.value: Popcorn, potato, pizza, vegetable, beverage, dinner plate

products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER 0.9 offers 900 W, ten power levels and preset buttons for popcorn, potato, pizza, frozen vegetable, beverage and dinner plate. It has a clock, a kitchen timer and a 30 second express button. A large LED display is easy to read.

At 900 W it is a clear step up from the 700 W units in speed. It is a good mid size for two people. Its six presets and ten levels at 900 W suit two people.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Check how to release the child lock. Use microwave safe containers in the BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave and stir food halfway, because cold spots are normal in any model at this price.
products.bestFor: Couples who want 900 W and presets

products.name: Chefman countertop microwave 0.9 cu ft, 900 W, 10 power levels
products.description:
The Chefman 0.9 is a 900 W digital microwave with ten power levels and six one touch presets. It offers express cooking buttons. It packs 900 W in a compact body.

It sits beside the BLACK+DECKER 0.9 as a near match. Choose between them on the preset list and the look. It is a near match to the BLACK+DECKER with a different preset list.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Wipe the cavity of the Chefman 0.9 microwave after spatters, as baked on residue spreads odours and can cause arcing near the waveguide cover.
products.bestFor: Couples who want a digital 900 W unit

products.name: COMFEE countertop microwave 0.7 cu ft, 700 W, ECO mode
products.description:
The COMFEE is a compact 0.7 cubic foot microwave at 700 W with one touch buttons, a two step child lock and an ECO mode. Its mute function silences the beep after three seconds of holding the sound button. It is the plain, small unit of the lineup.

At 700 W it cooks slowly, so package times need adding. It suits reheating, drinks and snacks more than full meals. Its 0.7 cu ft and 700 W make it the plain reheater.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. Check how to release the child lock. Keep the manual for the COMFEE 0.7 microwave, since the child lock and mute sequences differ between brands and are easy to trigger by accident.
products.bestFor: Dorm, office and single person reheating
cons: 700 W is slow for full meals

products.name: Commercial Chef 0.6 cu ft microwave, mechanical dial, 700 W
products.description:
The Commercial Chef is a 0.6 cubic foot microwave with mechanical dial controls, 700 W and six power levels. It has a pull handle door. The dial is simple and has little to fail.

It is the smallest cavity here and the plainest control style. It suits someone who sets a time and walks away. Its mechanical dial beats every digital panel on simplicity.

Wipe the cavity after spatters and keep the vents clear. The dial rarely needs attention. Do not run the Commercial Chef 0.6 microwave empty or with metal or foil inside, because both can damage the magnetron or cause arcing.
products.bestFor: Simple use with no digital panel
pros: Mechanical dial has little to fail

buyingCriteria.explanation: The beep after a cycle can be loud, and a mute option fixes that for night use. Eco modes cut standby power by dimming the display. TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave and Chefman 0.9 microwave are worth comparing on those details. These are small things that matter in a small apartment.

Ten power levels and a defrost by weight or time let you thaw without cooking the edges. Cheaper microwaves pulse full power on and off, which is harsh on frozen food. Farberware 1.1 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave offer different presets. Use lower power and stir or rest food to even out the heat.

Mechanical dials last long with little to fail, while digital panels add presets and a clock. A dial is simple to use and cheap to make, and a digital panel suits people who want popcorn and potato buttons. TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave (0.9 cu ft, 900 W) and Chefman 0.9 microwave (0.9 cu ft, 900 W) sit on different sides. Choose the control style you will use daily.

A child lock stops a unit from starting without a deliberate sequence, which helps in homes with young children. A door that opens with a push button or a pull handle is a matter of taste and accessibility. Farberware 1.1 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave list child lock in this lineup. Check how the lock is released before you rely on it.

A microwave needs space on the sides and top for its vents, and a unit jammed into a tight shelf runs hot. Compact units give up cavity for footprint. TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave and Chefman 0.9 microwave show the size spread in this lineup. Measure the counter and the clearance before ordering.

A one year warranty is typical, and the magnetron and the door latch are the usual failure points. A cheap unit is often cheaper to replace than to repair. Farberware 1.1 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave are covered by the standard period. Keep the receipt and register the product.

specDecoder.meaning: The size of the cavity. Small is about 0.5 to 0.9, midsize 1.1 to 1.7 and large 1.7 to 2.2.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check how BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave states its cavity and turntable size.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of steps between low and full power. Ten levels give finer control for defrosting.
specDecoder.watchFor: Note which of Farberware 1.1 microwave and TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave gives ten levels.

specDecoder.meaning: A button that starts 30 seconds at full power and adds 30 seconds on each press. It is the most used button on many units.
specDecoder.watchFor: Check whether Chefman 0.9 microwave offers it.

specDecoder.meaning: Output watts describe how much microwave energy reaches the food. Input power is higher, and the label times assume the output rating.
specDecoder.watchFor: Compare Farberware 1.1 microwave with TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave on output watts, not input watts.

specDecoder.meaning: Buttons that set time and power for popcorn, pizza or potatoes. They save guesswork but are not essential.
specDecoder.watchFor: Read the preset list for BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and presets
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at dial versus digital controls, preset lists and power levels. We favoured units whose controls match their price. BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave and Chefman 0.9 microwave represent different approaches in the lineup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and placement
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at footprint, turntable size and ventilation notes. A unit that fits a counter and a plate gets used. Farberware 1.1 microwave was the reference for a different size class.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: Recurring themes in owner feedback mattered to us, not a single headline number. Repeated complaints about noise, door latches or uneven heating lowered a pick. Ratings and review tallies are deliberately absent, and they played no part in the order here.

howWeEvaluated.title: Wattage and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated wattage and cavity size, using the rule that about 1000 to 1250 W suits meals. We ranked how well each unit matched a household. Farberware 1.1 microwave at 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W and TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave at 0.9 cu ft, 900 W were compared this way.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for child lock, mute and a pull or push door. These small features matter in busy households. TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave was compared against the others on this point.

howToChoose.intro: Decide first how much counter and cabinet space you can spare, since a microwave also needs ventilation clearance. Then decide whether you reheat leftovers or actually cook. The rows below map common situations to the picks in this lineup, including TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave.

rows: You want a compact 900 W unit
You want a digital 900 W unit
You want a dial and nothing else

howToChoose.note: Whichever you choose, measure the space including ventilation clearance, and check that your biggest plate actually turns inside the cavity.

howToChoose.intro: Every pick here is listed at or below the $100 cap, so the tiers below are relative to each other, not to the cap.

rows: Spending the least this lineup allows
COMFEE 0.7 microwave (0.7 cu ft, 700 W) costs the least in this lineup, so it suits a buyer who wants reheating and little else.
BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave (0.9 cu ft, 900 W) sits mid lineup on cost, balancing power, capacity and controls.
Farberware 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) costs the most in this lineup, so it needs to earn that premium on wattage, capacity or features.

howToChoose.note: Treat the tiers as relative: the cheapest pick suits reheating, the middle suits everyday cooking and the top of the lineup suits families.

cards.label: Digital controls and presets
cards.text: The group of Farberware 1.1 microwave, TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave, BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave, Chefman 0.9 microwave, and COMFEE 0.7 microwave uses a digital panel with presets. It offers popcorn, potato and beverage buttons, a clock and a timer. It suits people who like one touch cooking.

cards.label: Dial or simple controls
cards.text: The group of Commercial Chef 0.6 microwave uses a simpler control. A dial is cheap, long lasting and easy to use. It suits people who set a time and walk away.

howToChoose.note: Pick digital if you use presets daily. Pick a dial or simple panel if you want something that will not confuse anyone in the house.

rows: You reheat single plates, coffee and snacks in a small kitchen or dorm
COMFEE 0.7 microwave and Commercial Chef 0.6 microwave
A 0.6 to 0.7 cubic foot unit fits a counter corner and handles mugs and small bowls, but a full dinner plate may not turn freely.
You cook for two and want 900 W without a large footprint
TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave, BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave, and Chefman 0.9 microwave
A 0.9 cubic foot unit at 900 W is the practical middle: fast enough for meals and still compact.
You cook for a family and use full size plates and dishes
A 1.1 cubic foot or larger unit at 1000 W or more fits a standard dinner plate and cooks faster and more evenly than a small one.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for at least 900 W, a turntable that clears your biggest plate, a quick express button and a mute option. Ten power levels help with defrost. Those features matter more than a long preset list.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: Farberware 1.1 microwave is the pick that best matches those points here, with 1.1 cu ft, 1000 W. TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave and BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave are the nearest alternatives if you want a different size or a different mix of controls.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you cook for a family or want a sensor and a larger cavity. Stepping up to Farberware 1.1 microwave (1.1 cu ft, 1000 W) buys the wattage or size that cheaper units lack.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you reheat leftovers and drinks for one or two. COMFEE 0.7 microwave (0.7 cu ft, 700 W) covers the basics, and a small difference in features rarely justifies a larger premium.

maintenance.why: A worn cord is a fire risk. Replace any unit with a frayed or warm cord.
Without food to absorb energy, the magnetron can overheat. Keep a cup of water inside when testing.

maintenance.task: Clean the door seal and latch
maintenance.why: Residue on the seal can stop the door closing fully. A clean seal also keeps the cavity sealed.
Dust and clutter block airflow and make the unit run hot. Leave space on the sides and top.
Baked on food spreads odours and can cause arcing. A damp cloth and a bowl of steam loosen most residue.

faq.q: Is a bigger microwave always better?
faq.a: Not always, since a big cavity needs counter space and a large turntable. It does fit full plates, which a small unit may not. Measure your biggest plate before choosing, as the picks like BLACK+DECKER 0.9 microwave show.

faq.q: How long should a microwave last?
faq.a: With care many last several years, but the magnetron and door latch are the common failures. A cheap unit is often cheaper to replace than to repair. A sturdier unit like Chefman 0.9 microwave gives a little more headroom.

faq.q: Why does my food heat unevenly?
faq.a: Microwaves create hot and cold spots, which is normal. Stir food halfway, rest it for a minute and use lower power for dense items. A larger turntable helps.

faq.q: Is a child lock worth having?
faq.a: Yes in homes with young children, since it stops the oven starting without a deliberate sequence. Check how to release it. Most units here include one.

faq.q: Do I need a mechanical dial or digital panel?
faq.a: A dial is simple and long lasting, and a digital panel adds presets and a clock. Choose what you will use. Farberware 1.1 microwave and TOSHIBA 0.9 microwave show both approaches in this guide.

faq.q: Why does this guide stop at $100?
faq.a: The $100 cap is the search keyword shoppers use, and every pick here was listed at or below it when this guide was updated. COMFEE 0.7 microwave is the cheapest option in this lineup and Farberware 1.1 microwave is the dearest, so the spread inside the cap is real. Prices move, so check the listing before you buy.
